messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cont-batch pool kvcache memory amplification detected on cluster-us-east-1. Observed sustained growth in kvcache entries leading to page-in thrash and increased p99 latency for generate endpoints. Auto-escalation: P1. Root ts=2967778888

dave_oncall: On it — I'm seeing paging + ~40% latency increase for a subset of gen requests. Which config changed? :eyes:

emma_prod: Not aware of config roll. We did push a model rollout earlier today but that shouldn't touch batching configs. Customer-facing errors: some requests returning 504s from proxy (upstream timeout).

ray_infra: Logs show continuous-batching workers holding a lot more KV entries per batch. Looks like max_num_seqs was effectively bumped due to a bad default in the config template (0 -> interpreted unbounded).

jess_support: Customer impact: two mid-market tenants (acct:acme, acct:brightlabs) reporting timeouts and slow responses since 09:24 UTC. Support is collecting traces.

infra-bot: system: node-group cont-batch-frontend-5 autoscaler triggered scale-up +3 replicas at 09:27 UTC

incident-bot: Incident channel created, paging primary oncall dave_oncall, escalation to infra (ray_infra) and support (jess_support).

dave_oncall: Quick triage plan: 1) pin batch config to safe defaults (max_batch_tokens=1024, max_num_seqs=64, batch_timeout_ms=50) 2) enable KV eviction aggressive policy (eviction_target=0.65) 3) temporary route traffic away from affected nodes. Who can push?

ray_infra: I'll push the config hotfix to the cont-batch deployment now. Running command: ```kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/cont-batch CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024 CONTBATCH_MAX_NUM_SEQS=64 CONTBATCH_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=50``` will restart pods sequentially. Also applying kv eviction: ```redwoodctl apply -f - <<EOF
kind: KVCachingPolicy
name: cont-batch-emergency
eviction_target: 0.65
EOF```

emma_prod: Good. After we flip, we should monitor kvcache size and paging rates. Dashboards: /d/contbatch/perf -> watch kvcache_entries, page_faults/sec, p99_gen_latency.

jess_support: Noted. I told accounts to expect reduced throughput for a few mins while we roll. They asked for ETA. dave?

dave_oncall: ETA ~8-12 minutes for zero-downtime rolling restarts. I'll update externally after metrics show recovery.

ray_infra: Hotfix applied to 6/8 pods (rolling). Observed immediate drop in kvcache median entries on the patched pods. page_faults/sec down by ~70% on those pods. Patching remaining pods.

incident-bot: automation: Canary analysis: success (latency restored) on canary group at 09:33 UTC. Proceeding with full rollout.

jess_support: acme confirms timeouts have stopped but still seeing elevated latency for some long-context requests.

dave_oncall: That's expected — aggressive eviction will force some prefix recompute on first request. Should normalize as caches warm. We'll consider a gradual cache size correction later.

ray_infra: Full rollout complete at 09:36 UTC. kvcache entries down cluster-wide, page_faults/sec back to baseline, p99 latency dropping toward normal. Rolling restart introduced small blips but no sustained errors.

emma_prod: Customer impact summary (temp): ~12 minutes of elevated p99/504s for two tenants; approx 0.8% of total gen requests had 504s during window. Marking severity as mitigated; continue monitoring for 1h.

jess_support: Logged support ticket numbers and notified account reps. Customers requested root cause and timeline; we'll draft a follow-up.

dave_oncall: Next steps: 1) schedule postmortem with infra + runtime (include config templating change) 2) add guardrail to config validation to reject max_num_seqs=0/unset 3) add metric alert for KV amplification (growth rate threshold + paging spike) 4) include a canary check for batching config changes.

ray_infra: I also pushed an immediate config lint in the repo: `scripts/validate_batch_config.py` updated to fail CI if max_num_seqs missing or <=0. Pushing PR now.

infra-bot: ci: PR #4721 created by ray_infra - validate_batch_config CI checks pending.

dave_oncall: Nice. I'll leave the channel open for 1h monitoring and then hand off to oncall rotation. If anything regresses @emma_prod please ping. :thumbsup:

jess_support: Thanks team. I'll coordinate the customer incident email with engineering notes and mitigation steps.

emma_prod: Note for postmortem: include timeline, affected tenants, metric graphs (kvcache entries, page_faults/sec, p99), config diff, and remediation PRs. Assign owners: ray_infra (root cause), dave_oncall (mitigation), jess_support (customer comms).

incident-bot: incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated, monitor. Created incident ticket INC-2026-0742.

dave_oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m; handoff to next oncall (emma_prod) at 10:10 UTC.

emma_prod: I'll take watch. Thanks.

jess_support: Filed follow-up for postmortem and customer notes. Closing channel after monitoring period. :white_check_mark:
